out:
{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that an experimental manipulation designed to implicitly prime analytic thinking would reduce belief in conspiracy theories compared to a control condition.",
  "design": "between",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "A scrambled sentence verbal fluency task containing target words related to analytic or rational reasoning (e.g., 'analyse', 'reason', 'ponder', 'think', 'rational') versus neutral words in the control condition.",
  "outcome_measure": "Belief in Conspiracy Theories Inventory (BCTI), a 15-item scale measuring general conspiracist ideation.",
  "population_and_setting": "Undergraduate students at a university in London, UK.",
  "sample_size_total": 112,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Students enrolled in an introductory psychology course; participation was voluntary.",
  "analysis_plan": "A 2 (experimental condition: Analytic vs. Control) x 2 (Testing Session: Pre-manipulation vs. Post-manipulation) repeated measures ANOVA.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants completed the BCTI several weeks before and immediately after the priming task. The priming task was presented as a 'verbal fluency' task to mask the study hypothesis. A pilot study was conducted to validate that the priming procedure elicited analytic processing using the Moses Illusion task."
}
